messages.subject: Bioconductor teaching committee meeting, March 8
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

quick reminder about the Bioconductor teaching committee meeting on Monday, March 8, 2pm CET. Jitsi link as usual: https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching. Based on the discussion below, I think that the data set selection for the lessons would benefit from some more discussion in this meeting. If you have additional topics, please feel free to add them to the agenda.

See you on Monday!
Charlotte

> On 25 Feb 2021, at 05:41, Drnevich, Jenny <drne...@illinois.edu> wrote:
>

> Aaron pointed me to a promising data set: scRNAseq::BachMammaryData(). 25K cells total from 4 mammary developmental stages, 2 replicates each!  I made an attempt at reading in the data, getting logNormCounts, pulling 13 genes I got from skimming the paper (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-02001-5), transposing the normalized values to cells X genes and then adding on colData. This has all 25,806 cell barcodes from Cell Ranger; the paper clearly lays out the extra cell filtering thresholds, but they only ended up filtering out ~800 cells so I did not bother to try it.  I also did not attempt any plotting at all to see if these genes were suitable – time for me to go to bed.
>
>
>
> Knitting takes about ~5 min for me, mostly due to the normalization but downloading the data the first time could add on more. I’m fairly old-school with base R coding so feel free to update to “tidyr” ways. I did put it in a tibble at the end! The final .csv and .rds are < 1500 KB, an easy size for downloading
>
>
>
> I pushed everything to  https://github.com/Bioconductor/bioconductor-teaching/tree/master/data/BachMammaryData
>
>
>
> Goodnight,
>
> Jenny
>
>
>
> From: bioconduct...@googlegroups.com <bioconduct...@googlegroups.com> On Behalf Of Drnevich, Jenny
> Sent: Wednesday, February 24, 2021 3:56 PM
> To: lauren...@gmail.com <http://gmail.com> <lauren...@gmail.com>; bioconductor-teaching <bioconduct...@googlegroups.com>
> Subject: RE: (sc)RNA-Seq data for intro course
>
>
>
> I’ve asked Aaron Lun on the singlecell-queries slack. He was looking for data sets for his data package.
>
>
>
> Jenny
>
>
>
> From:  bioconduct...@googlegroups.com <bioconduct...@googlegroups.com> On Behalf Of lauren...@gmail.com
> Sent: Wednesday, February 24, 2021 3:19 PM
> To: bioconductor-teaching <bioconduct...@googlegroups.com>
> Subject: (sc)RNA-Seq data for intro course
>
>
>
> Dear all,
>
>
>
> I have looked more closely at the snRNASeq and RNASeq datasets with the goal of formatting them for the intro course (i.e. make them similar in structure to the ecology surveys data).
>
>
>
> - As already discussed, the wide format with genes by sample with the row data cbinded isn't appropriate at all.
>
>
>
> - I initially thought that taking a subset of genes, pivoting that into a long format and joining that with the colData would work, but it doesn't at all. That data fails at the very first plotting exercise, where we want to produce a scatter plot of one gene vs another one. This is only possible if we pivot the data back into a wide format, to recover genes as columns. Even though pivot_wider() and pivot_longer() have been introduced before starting the plotting chapter, I feel it leads to a cognitive overload for students, who need to understand pivoting to re-format the data they have familiarised themselves before being able to learn ggplot2.
>
>
>
> - The type of data that would work would be to start from the assay for a handful of genes, transpose that to have n samples along the rows and sample names + handful of genes as columns, and then join this with the colData. I think this would exactly match what we would need to re-use the flow of the data carpentry lesson.
>
>
>
> - Unfortunately, this approach generates datasets with 45 (bulk) or 384 (scRNA) rows, which is too small to really make a strong case for using R for data analysis. Compare this against the 30K+ rows of the surveys data.
>
>
>
> Are you aware of a (sc)RNA-Seq dataset with 10K+ samples, ideally with a time component?
>
>
>
> Best wishes,
>
>
>
> Laurent
>
> --

messages.subject: Presentation submission for BioC2021 by March 16th!
messages.subject_clean: Presentation submission for BioC2021 by March 16th!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

One thing we forgot to talk about yesterday – doing some sort of presentation at BioC2021. The deadline for submissions has been extended to March 16th ( https://bioc2021.bioconductor.org/submissions/).  Do we think we will have the Intro to R workshop in good enough shape to present part of it as a long workshop (1.5 – 2 hrs)? That could be a good way to test it out and get lots of feedback. I remember that there often were short talks on a topic with “come to our workshop to learn more” and or we could possibly also put in for a Birds of a Feather for after the workshop to discuss teaching/training issues? I would be happy to take the lead on doing the submission depending on what every thinks we can do.

Best,

Jenny

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Jenny - I agree that we should do something. Maybe one possibility could be a “joint material development session” or something like that, where we invite people to contribute to/comment on the developed material, start drawing up new possible lessons (or find a group of like-minded to do it with), or discuss what lessons might be useful? I guess this could qualify as a birds-of-a-feather session, or even a long workshop? I also agree that it could probably be useful to submit a similar short talk as for EuroBioc, to make more people aware of the efforts.
Charlotte

messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I have a draft of the Workshop submission syllabus (html attached). Location on github:

https://github.com/jdrnevich/BuildACarpentriesWorkshop/blob/master/vignettes/CarpentriesWorkshopSyllabus.Rmd

Feel free to edit heavily if you can – it is really rough shape right now and I realized how much work we will need to do not only on developing this “lesson sprint” workshop but also the main Introduction to R workshop. In skimming through the Curriculum Development handbook, the Chapter on Curriculum structure lays out episodes vs. lessons vs. curriculum (https://cdh.carpentries.org/our-curriculum-structure.html). If the Introduction to R is going to be an entire curriculum, then most of our efforts so far have been more focused on the data import, cleaning and visualization. I tried to broaden this out to include a standard data organization and management section. It shouldn’t be that hard to modify these concepts from the Ecology or Genomics curricula to fit our -omics based data set.

Having never submitted to run a BioC workshop before, I am not sure how acceptable this rough syllabus will be. Anyone with experience, please chime in with what area needs to be the main focus for improvement before the submission deadline in approximately 24 hours from now (for me).

Thanks,

Jenny
